text: .29. The opioid antagonist naloxone may also improve blood pressure in shock,30 but its role is not established. Specific therapies are indicated in some types of shock. In cardiogenic shock associated with myocardial infarc- tion,2,31 specific therapy to restore myocardial perfusion is also required (see p.1175). In septic shock appropriate antibacterial therapy should be given as outlined under Septicaemia on p.190. Methods of inhibiting endogenous mediators released in response to sepsis that are thought to be responsible for the haemody- namic effects are also under investigation but clinical benefits have not yet been shown.3,32 However, improved outcomes have been reported33,34 with the use of low-dose corticosteroids, and in severe sepsis activated protein C may also be used.6 Adrenaline is the cornerstone of management in anaphy- lactic shock (see p.1205). 1.
